note: The weekly loop's first challengers, from the research (19 Nov 2026): what the research was unsure of, ranked, alternating first-second and look tests.

candidates.test: frame 1 is the document with the figure already highlighted, against the champion's object-first frame (the toy, the cup)
candidates.why: KFC (591K, the owner's favourite) opens on a report table with a cell highlighted; Labubu (2.28M) and Stanley open on the object. 2 of 3 breakout openings are object-first, so the object is champion

candidates.test: the bed ~36 dB under the voice against the champion's ~32 dB
candidates.why: the references span 22 dB (KFC) to 36.5 dB (Labubu, Company Man ~36); 32 is a midpoint, not a measurement of what holds viewers
the scan's on-niche Shorts under 35 s have a 54,049 median (81) vs 23,214 at 35-70 s, but the Shorts that broke out (Rise Fall Repeat) run 106-147 s; the build spec asks to test longer

candidates.test: long videos with no chapter cards (continuous narration with date slams) against 4-5 s chapter cards with a music drop
candidates.why: KFC uses 5 cards and Labubu 9; Modern MBA none; a silent 4-5 s card is also where long-video viewers may leave

candidates.test: a Short whose title and first line ask the question ('Why did everyone stop buying Crocs?') against the champion's paradox claim
candidates.why: the build spec says a claim, never a question, from 4 Rise Fall Repeat Shorts; style.json shows 1 of 4 Shorts opening on a question; thin evidence either way

candidates.test: Shorts with every figure only in the captions (no gold poster card) against the poster card for the one big result
candidates.why: the poster card comes from one channel's Shorts (Rise Fall Repeat); the other references show figures in captions only

candidates.test: long titles of the form 'What Happened to X?' / 'WTF Happened to X?' against a claim title ('Beanie Babies Were Supposed to Pay for College')
candidates.why: the biggest small-channel breakout was 'WTF Happened to Labubu?' (2.28M on 6.5K subs) and 'what happened to brand' is one of the niche's searches; our first titles are mostly claims

candidates.test: stock footage 55-60% with graphics 10-15% (KFC's mix) against the champion's 35-45% footage and 20-25% graphics
candidates.why: KFC ran ~60% stock and ~6% graphics; Fortune & Fall ~40% and ~25%; the champion bets on graphics as our edge, unproven on our own videos
